No. 2 of 2026
AN ACT to amend the Income Tax Act, Cap. 15.02 and for
related matters.
[ 19th February, 2026 ]
BE IT ENACTED by the King’s Most Excellent Majesty, by
and with the advice and consent of the House of Assembly and Senate
of Saint Lucia, and by the authority of the same, as follows:

10
No. 2 ] Income Tax (Amendment) Act [ 2026
Short title
1. This Act may be cited as the Income Tax (Amendment) Act,
2026.
Interpretation
2. In this Act, “principal Act” means the Income Tax Act, Cap.
15.02.
Amendment of section 38
3. Section 38(1) of the principal Act is amended —
(a) by deleting paragraph (v) and substituting the following —
“(v)for the income years 2023 to 2025, the entire
expenditure related to the purchase and installation
of a solar photovoltaic system or related components
in the income year incurred and where a deduction is
allowed under this paragraph, there is no deduction
in respect to capital expenditure under section 40 and
Schedule 2 for the same solar photovoltaic system or
related components;”;
(b) by inserting immediately after paragraph (v) the following
new paragraph (w) —
“(w) in any income year, expenditure related to
investments in cyber security, artificial intelligence
tools and information and communication technology
training for staff as specified by the Comptroller and
the deduction in respect of expenditure up to fifty
thousand dollars.”.
Amendment of section 44
4. Section 44 of the principal Act is amended by deleting
subsection (4) and substituting the following —
“(4) Notwithstanding this Act —
(a) effective from the 1st day of January, 2025 the
aggregate allowances and deductions permitted under

11
No. 2 ] Income Tax (Amendment) Act [ 2026
Parts 6 and 7, excluding the personal allowance and
deduction for medical expenses must not exceed forty
thousand dollars;
(b) in the case of income year 2025 the allowances and
deductions excluded from the overall cap of forty
thousand dollars are —
(i) the personal allowance,
(ii) the deduction for medical expenses, and
(iii)the expenses relating to the purchase and
installation of solar photovoltaic systems or
related components.”.
Amendment of section 48
5. Section 48 of the principal Act is amended —
(a) by deleting subsection (1) and substituting the following —
“(1) From the 1st day of January, 2025 and subject to this
section, in ascertaining the chargeable income of an
individual who is resident in Saint Lucia and who proves
to the satisfaction of the Comptroller that he or she
maintained a child who —
(a) was born during the income year; or
(b) at the commencement of the income year has not
attained the age of sixteen years or, irrespective
of age, was a student or an invalid child,
is entitled to a deduction of five thousand dollars.”;
(b) by deleting subsection (2) and substituting the following —
“(2) From the 1st day of January, 2025, the deductable
allowance under this section does not apply in relation to
any child whose income from any source during the
income year exceeds five thousand dollars.”.

12
No. 2 ] Income Tax (Amendment) Act [ 2026
Amendment of section 49
6. Section 49 of the principal Act is amended by deleting
subsection (2) and substituting the following —
“(2) From the 1st day of January, 2025, the deduction allowable
under this section is five thousand dollars in respect of any
one child.”.
Amendment of section 50
7. Section 50 of the principal Act is amended by deleting
subsection (2) and substituting the following —
“(2) From the 1st day of January, 2025, the deduction
allowable under this section is ten thousand dollars in respect
of any one person.”.
Amendment of section 52
8. Section 52 of the principal Act is amended —
(a) by deleting subsection (1) and substituting the following —
“(1) From the 1st day of January, 2025 and subject to
this section, where a resident individual during the year
of income maintains a dependent relative he or she is
entitled to an allowance of five thousand dollars, in respect
of each such relative.”;
(b) in subsection (2), by deleting paragraph (b) and substituting
the following —
“(b) shall be reduced, from the 1st day of January, 2025,
where such dependent relative has assessable income
in excess of five thousand dollars, by one dollar for
each dollar of the excess.”.
Amendment of section 54
9. Section 54 of the principal Act is amended by deleting —
(a) subsection (1) and substituting the following —
“(1) From the 1st day of January, 2025, a resident
individual is entitled to a deduction in respect of any

13
No. 2 ] Income Tax (Amendment) Act [ 2026
amount paid during the year of income with respect to the
following —
(a) subject to subsections (2) and (3), interest on
money borrowed by him or her and applied for the
acquisition or construction of, or improvements
to an owner occupied dwelling house;
(b) taxes incurred in respect of an owner occupied
dwelling house;
(c) insurance premiums on an owner occupied
dwelling house;
(d) expenses reasonably incurred in the upkeep and
maintenance of an owner occupied dwelling
house, and the deduction allowable for any year
of income in respect of such expenditure must not
exceed ten thousand dollars.”;
(b) subsection (1A) and substituting the following —
“(1A) Notwithstanding subsection (1)(a), the deduction
allowable for homeowners with respect to
interest on money borrowed and applied for the acquisition
or construction of an owner occupied dwelling house from
the 1st day of January, 2025 must not exceed forty
thousand dollars.”;
(c) subsection (1B) and substituting the following —
“(1B) The maximum deduction allowable on mortgage
interest under subsection (1)(a) applies to homeowners
from the 1st day of January, 2025 and must
not exceed forty thousand dollars.”.
Amendment of section 56
10. Section 56 of the principal Act is amended —
(a) in subsection (1) by deleting the words “sections 45, 46,
48, 49, 50 or 51” and substituting the words “sections
45, 46, 48, 49, 50, 51 or 52”;

14
No. 2 ] Income Tax (Amendment) Act [ 2026
(b) in subsection (3), by deleting paragraph (a) of the definition
of the words “medical expenses” and substituting the
following —
“(a) to a registered medical practitioner, a qualified
nurse or a midwife, a chemist or to a hospital or
other similar institution for services or facilities
provided or medicines prescribed by a registered
medical practitioner for the treatment of any illness
or in connection with the birth of a child or fertility
treatment;”.
Amendment of section 57
11. Section 57 of the principal Act is amended by deleting
subsection (1) and substituting the following —
“(1) From the 1st day of January, 2025 and subject to this
section, where in any year of income a resident individual
makes payments by way of subscription for shares in any
society registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, Cap.
12.06 or incorporated under the Building Societies Act, Cap.
12.04 there is allowed a deduction for such payments up to a
limit of ten thousand dollars.”.
Substitution of section 59
12. The principal Act is amended by deleting section 59 and
substituting the following —
“Deduction for investments
59.—(1) From the 1st day of January, 2025
and subject to this section, where in any income year,
a resident individual invests in any security instruments,
including treasury bills, treasury notes, bonds, shares and
mutual funds, issued by a local or regional institution, he or
she is entitled to a deduction.
(2) The deductable allowance under this section is equivalent
to the value of the investment purchased up to a limit of ten
thousand dollars in an income year.”.

15
No. 2 ] Income Tax (Amendment) Act [ 2026
Amendment of section 63
13. Section 63 of the principal Act is amended by deleting
subsection (14) and substituting the following —
“(14) Where cash benefits are payable to a member under
subsection (12) or (13) on withdrawal from a pension fund
such moneys shall not form part of the chargeable income of
the member but shall be separately charged to tax in the hands
of the trustees who shall deduct, as penalty, ten per cent of
the moneys prior to payment of the balance to the member.”.
Passed in the House of Assembly this 3rd day of February, 2026.
CLAUDIUS J. FRANCIS,
Speaker of the House of Assembly.
Passed in the Senate this 10th day of February, 2026.
ALVINA REYNOLDS,
President of the Senate.
